6.7 Hydraulic Cylinder and Component Remanufacturing Quality Inspection Methods
6.7.1 Hydraulic Cylinder and Component Remanufacturing Pre-Production Quality Inspection Methods
According to GB/T 28619-2012 regulations, remanufactured hydraulic cylinders and their components are referred to as remanufactured blanks.

The purpose of quality inspection of hydraulic cylinders and their components before remanufacturing is to: based on the appearance of the remanufactured blank, internal defects and special performance test results, assess whether the remanufactured blank can be remanufactured. Under certain conditions, the remanufacturing enterprise may conduct remaining life assessment. Based on the assessment of the blank's remaining design life at the remanufacturing stage, and the results of failure mode analysis, using non-destructive testing technology to determine the remanufactured blank's life aging laws and degradation levels, establishing service life reference parameters based on the degree of damage to the remanufactured blank, and evaluating the remaining life of the remanufactured blank.

For remanufactured blanks that are not allowed to have potential hazardous defects, and for remanufactured blanks with latent hazardous defects, refer to Table 6-23 for early damage detection methods. Based on non-destructive testing and the specific characteristics of the aging and degradation process during detection, the early damage level is determined to predict the remaining life.

1. Application of Laser Cladding Remanufacturing Technology for Coal Mining Hydraulic Support Columns and Jack Cylinder Bores

The so-called coal mining hydraulic support column and jack cylinder bore laser cladding remanufacturing technology refers to the remanufacturing of columns and jacks whose chrome plating layer has peeled off, corrosion damage and other damage resulting in failure, by using laser cladding technology on stainless steel material to achieve or restore the original quality level of a new product.

According to reference [124], the laser cladding repair of column rods under coal mine working conditions has a lifespan of: chrome-plated repaired column rods have a service life of 1-1.5 years; laser cladding repaired column rods still show no rust or corrosion after 4.5 years of use. According to simulation test results, the service life of laser cladding repaired columns used as the outer surface of hydraulic support columns should be 6 times the service life of the original chrome-plated columns.

According to DB 37/T 1932-2011 regulations, the column and jack bottom should mainly be cleaned of rust, oil stains, degreasing treatment, and judged suitable for remanufacturing based on the following conditions. Those judged not suitable for remanufacturing:

items: a) For cylinder bodies, the gap between the small column seal and the mating surface radial depth should not exceed 2mm.
b) For cylinder bodies, the gap between the small column seal and the mating surface should not exceed a radial depth of 2mm.
c) Cylinder bodies with cracks, cracks at the cylinder end threaded connection or other connection parts that are incomplete.
d) The straightness deviation of the cylinder bore inner hole is greater than 0.05%; the cylindricity deviation is greater than 0.2% of the nominal dimension.
e) The straightness deviation of the piston rod is greater than 0.1%.

sections.text: For detailed part evaluation, please also refer to DB 37/T 2688.2-2015 and other standards.
DB 37/T 1932-2011 also specifies the requirements for key component laser cladding to remanufacture stainless steel columns and column sleeves. Main component pre-repair requirements:

For the outer cylinder body, the cylinder body, piston rod welding seam grade should meet GB/T 6402, GB/T 5777 requirements and pass ultrasonic flaw detection. If the outer cylinder body and cylinder body damage depth, width, and circumferential extent are severe, it is necessary to use laser cladding or electroplating process to repair the cylinder bore interior, meeting technical requirements.

Laser cladding remanufactured stainless steel column sleeve requirements: The laser cladding layer thickness should be no less than 0.5mm. After laser cladding, the surface hardness should be no less than 40HRC, and after pressure treatment the surface hardness should be no less than 42HRC. The cladding layer should be uniform and flat, with no cracks, no blistering, no peeling, no spattering or loosening, and should be free from scorch marks; the sealing groove and sealing surface should have no pitting or other external defects.
(1) Application of laser cladding technology on coal mine hydraulic support columns.

The hydraulic support column oil cylinder laser cladding necessity is described in reference [125]. The introduction states that Shanxi Xishan Mining Group's hydraulic support columns are large in size, with various types of jack repairs - one type uses electroplating technology. Based on environmental protection requirements, electroplating and chrome plating have been phased out by many factories over the years. The chrome plating price continues to rise, already becoming an alternative to hydraulic support columns. Jack repair restoration uses this method. Moreover, electrochrome plating cannot meet the needs of coal mine users, especially in environments with H₂S gas or acidic gas (or acidic mine water). The laser cladding layer's service life is 5 times that of electroplated chrome layers.

Currently, most domestic high-pressure hydraulic support columns use laser cladding repair. After laser cladding repair, the next repair timing is only when a casting defect or spot point appears, and the repair method is to apply a complete repair to all areas with base material removed, reducing time, labor costs, environmental pollution, and after laser cladding repair, under a single support column, the production time is reduced, large area columns do not need fracture treatment, and only need to re-clad the damaged point areas, significantly reducing time, costs, and environmental impact.

2) Using electroplating and laser cladding repair capabilities, the electroplating process involves depositing metal on the base material to form the plating layer or changing the base material surface to achieve chemical modification. Due to the harmful nature of the process, it is prone to pollution, easy to crack, easy to peel. The plating process also uses a combination of mixed alloys and additional hardened composite coating layers. The plating layer thickness is generally 0.05-0.06mm. The plating layer's hardness is relatively low. When subjected to pressure, shock or impact, the plating layer is easily scratched and cracked. In laboratory conditions, moisture in the air will pass through tiny cracks in the coating base material, and the coating will gradually deteriorate over time, resulting in the formation of reduced area coverage, with rust and corrosion spreading under the surface, thereby generating more surface area loss.
3) Economic analysis: According to research findings, laser cladding process cost is 3189.5 yuan/m², while electroplating process cost is 1450

yuan/m². Electroplating requires nickel pre-plating followed by chrome plating during each major repair, and laser cladding repair only requires small area patching during major repairs, so the laser cladding process saves significantly on subsequent maintenance costs. This effectively solves the problem of battery bottle neck issues encountered in the repair process of large support columns and jacks of various kinds.
(2) Application of Stainless Steel Powder Laser Cladding Remanufacturing Technology for Hydraulic Cylinder Rod Components

According to reference [126], an introduction and field investigation show that a certain hydraulic support bracket must be used in an environment where natural weather and harsh conditions prevail, resulting in high corrosion susceptibility. The hydraulic cylinder rod extends to its full stroke during operation, and is prone to bending and deformation. Due to overload, the piston rod's working condition is poor, and since there is excessive super-travel, the rod body surface shows peeling. Due to excessive stress, the rod body and seal bearing area are damaged, causing the seal to fail completely. Under the condition that the hydraulic cylinder rod is pressed, the cylinder sealing becomes tight, and if the grease is too much, the rod surface will appear to have two-thirds of the outer coating removed, and the coating material will remain on the rod surface.

The spray welding method is adopted. Due to chromium plating's hardness and ability to resist impact not being satisfactory, the laser cladding approach is used to improve the surface hardness of the hydraulic cylinder body rod. Stainless steel-based laser cladding remanufacturing process is applied to the hydraulic cylinder body rod's surface. The surface hardness, surface roughness reduction, and durability are improved, thus improving the service life of the hydraulic cylinder body's useful working range. Cost-effective economic benefits can be obtained.

Laser cladding of hydraulic cylinder rod components with stainless steel powder for restoration is a type of high-energy laser beam cladding process that achieves non-deformation of the area without causing heat distortion of the material. The process of reaching the surface hardening technique involves the basic principle of using a high-power density (10³-10⁵W/cm²) laser beam to irradiate the hydraulic cylinder rod surface. The irradiated surface layer area is rapidly heated to above the phase transformation critical temperature, and when the surface temperature of the workpiece reaches a temperature below the melting point, the stainless steel powder coated on the surface of the rod begins to melt. Due to the extremely fast cooling of the substrate, at a large temperature gradient, the heated zone rapidly cools from the austenitizing temperature. Since most of the workpiece acts as a heat conductor, the stainless steel melt rapidly solidifies. When the laser beam stops irradiating, the heated zone rapidly cools (10⁶-10⁸°C/s), and the substrate itself acts as a two-directional cooling medium, producing metallurgically bonded layers on the outer surface.
Using this stainless steel cladding remanufacturing technology to restore hydraulic cylinder rod components has the following characteristics:

items: 1) Laser beam provides rapid heating, self-cooling, no need for insulation and cooling treatment. It is a non-polluting green environmental heat treatment process. It can easily achieve laser cladding repair of the hydraulic cylinder rod surface.
2) Due to the fast laser heating speed, the heat-affected zone is small, which is surface scanning heating, so the repaired hydraulic cylinder rod deformation is minimal.

3) Due to the small laser beam divergence angle, it has good directionality, and can precisely guide the optical system to achieve local precision surface processing of hydraulic cylinder rod surfaces.

The biggest danger of hydraulic oil temperature being too high is that the hydraulic oil itself will eventually decompose, and the ability to maintain hydraulic oil viscosity and lubrication will be reduced. Various organic compounds may be deposited in the hydraulic oil in the form of oil sludge or paint (oxidized particles) such as asphalt, resin, carbon and other polymer compounds. These resinous and viscous substances may cause valves to stick, and rubber seal materials will also be degraded and hardened, leading to eventual damage and resulting in blockage of pore passages, orifices, and screen meshes.

In most cases, high-temperature oil combined with water and air causes more severe corrosion. Thinner oil may also increase wear due to greater impact and vibration, and may cause structural vibration, bearing loosening, and other damage. If lubricity is lost, the lubricating oil film is also lost, which causes contact between the metal of the cylinder and the metal surface to directly rub against each other, producing wear debris.

Temperature is a key factor in oil oxidation. Below 60°C, oxidation is negligible; above 60°C, the rate of chemical reaction approximately doubles for every 10°C increase. Above 60°C, the temperature further increases by 10°C and the life of the mineral oil decreases by about one-half, and at 100°C the useful life decreases to 97%.

Based on the above facts, the working temperature of the hydraulic system should ideally have a sufficient margin against oxidation reactions, keeping the hydraulic oil degradation to a minimum. However, the oil temperature is not necessarily the actual oil temperature, as the outlet temperature is the actual temperature, and local oxidation that is particularly severe in some areas also affects the overall surface condition.

Oil thermal stability refers to the ability of oil to resist decomposition caused by its own temperature. If the operating temperature exceeds the acceptable threshold for a prolonged period, the established maximum oil temperature limit is reached. It is worth noting that the vast majority of failures in hydraulic systems, especially in electro-hydraulic servo and proportional valve-controlled hydraulic cylinder control systems, are caused by hydraulic oil contamination. In particular, solid particles (contamination) cause the system to exhibit abnormal behavior and may present an otherwise unexplained failure. Therefore, the first concern should be whether the hydraulic oil contains solid particulate contamination.
7.2 Selection and Use of Hydraulic Cylinders
7.2.1 Selection of Hydraulic Cylinders
1. Hydraulic Cylinder Selection Guidelines

Reference [54] provides a guideline for hydraulic cylinder selection. Improper selection of hydraulic cylinders not only causes user economic losses and damage, but may also lead to accidents. The selection should be based on a comprehensive analysis of the working requirements, selection of appropriate structures and installation methods, combined with comprehensive reference parameters.
The main considerations when selecting hydraulic cylinders are:

items: 1) Cylinder bore and output force or cylinder bore diameter.
2) Nominal pressure (highest specified or rated) pressure and working pressure.
3) Cylinder stroke and piston rod diameter.
4) Maximum travel distance and cylinder working stroke range.
5) Reciprocating travel speed.
6) Installation method.
7) Environmental conditions (such as ambient temperature, site contamination, etc.).
8) Service life.
9) Appearance dimensions.
10) Working medium.
11) Sealing device.
12) Other devices (such as cushioning devices, exhaust (bleed), air release devices, etc.).

sections.text: When selecting hydraulic cylinders, priority should be given to using relevant national standards for hydraulic cylinders. This approach is not only reliable in quality, but first of all it has a large interchangeability advantage. Second, it is easy to provide spare parts, and it has the advantage of short delivery time. Other types of hydraulic cylinders should be designed and calculated according to the surrounding conditions, combined with test results and experience verification, using specialized production and manufacturing equipment, tooling, fixtures, and inspection tools to complete the process.
